sections.skill: Decide the truth of "all", "some" and "no" statements over a stated domain

questions.prompt: The domain is exactly these five club members: Ava (age 15, chess, has a bus pass), Ben (16, robotics, no bus pass), Cy (15, robotics, bus pass), Dee (17, chess, bus pass), Eli (16, art, no bus pass). "All chess members have a bus pass."

figure.description: A table of five club members with their age, club and whether they have a bus pass.

questions.prompt: The domain is exactly these five club members: Ava (age 15, chess, has a bus pass), Ben (16, robotics, no bus pass), Cy (15, robotics, bus pass), Dee (17, chess, bus pass), Eli (16, art, no bus pass). "Some member aged 16 has a bus pass."

figure.description: A table of five club members with their age, club and whether they have a bus pass.

questions.prompt: The domain is exactly these five club members: Ava (age 15, chess, has a bus pass), Ben (16, robotics, no bus pass), Cy (15, robotics, bus pass), Dee (17, chess, bus pass), Eli (16, art, no bus pass). Which statement is TRUE?

choices.text: All robotics members have a bus pass.
No art member has a bus pass.

questions.correct_answer: No art member has a bus pass.

figure.description: A table of five club members with their age, club and whether they have a bus pass.

questions.prompt: The domain is exactly these five club members: Ava (age 15, chess, has a bus pass), Ben (16, robotics, no bus pass), Cy (15, robotics, bus pass), Dee (17, chess, bus pass), Eli (16, art, no bus pass). How many members make "the member is 15 or has no bus pass" true?

figure.description: A table of five club members with their age, club and whether they have a bus pass.

questions.prompt: The domain is the whole numbers 1 to 10. Which statement is FALSE?

choices.text: Some number in the domain is prime.
Every number in the domain is less than 10.
Some number in the domain is a multiple of 7.
No number in the domain is negative.

questions.correct_answer: Every number in the domain is less than 10.

sections.relationship: Each quantifier makes a different claim; students who read "some" as "all" (or "no" as "not all") misjudge truth.
sections.author_note: Each quantifier makes a different claim; students who read "some" as "all" (or "no" as "not all") misjudge truth.

questions.prompt: "Some students walk to school" is true when ...

choices.text: at least one student walks to school

questions.correct_answer: at least one student walks to school

questions.prompt: "No student walks to school" is true when ...
"All the lights are on" is true if exactly one light is off.
"Some numbers in {2, 4, 6} are odd" is true.
"Every number in {3, 5, 7} is odd" is true.

sections.relationship: A quantified statement is about the stated domain only. Students who think of numbers or people outside it get the wrong truth value.
sections.author_note: A quantified statement is about the stated domain only. Students who think of numbers or people outside it get the wrong truth value.

questions.prompt: The domain is {1, 2, 3}. "Every number in the domain is less than 4" is true.
The domain is {10, 20, 30}. "Some number in the domain is odd" is true.
The domain is the days Monday to Friday. Which is true?

choices.text: No day in the domain is a weekend day.
Every day in the domain starts with M.
Some day in the domain is Sunday.
Some day in the domain is Saturday.

questions.correct_answer: No day in the domain is a weekend day.

questions.prompt: "All prime numbers are odd" is true when the domain is {3, 5, 7, 11}.
"All prime numbers are odd" is true when the domain is all whole numbers.

sections.relationship: Expert: "for every ... there is ..." and the order of quantifiers.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: The domain is the whole numbers 1 to 5. "For every number x, there is a number y with y > x" is true.
The domain is the whole numbers 1 to 5. "There is a number y such that for every number x, y ≥ x" is true.
The domain is all whole numbers. Which statement is TRUE?

choices.text: For every x and every y, y > x.
There is an x such that for every y, y > x.
For every x, there is a y with y > x.
There is a y such that for every x, y > x.

questions.correct_answer: For every x, there is a y with y > x.

questions.prompt: The domain is the whole numbers 1 to 9. Give a number x that makes "for every y in the domain, x + y > 5" true.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: x >= 5 and x <= 9 and isInteger(x) (example: x = 6)
